title: Treasury cash-management buyback operation (1Mo-2Y nominal, $12.5B cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/8/2026, operation 9/9/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/10/2026, Cash Management, Nominal Coupons 1Mo to 2Y, maturity range 10/10/2026 - 09/09/2028, min $0, max $12.5 billion. Stays estimate on the two counts the sibling treasury-buyback-7y10y-2026-09-17 proposal already documented: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-08 operation announcement rather than this document, checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-20y-bond-2026-09-15 D-7 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), reading the schedule PDF for that ledger's own long-end buyback question. WHY IT EARNS A SLOT: this calendar tracks every long-end LIQUIDITY-SUPPORT operation (treasury-buyback-10y20y-*, treasury-buyback-20y30y-*, treasury-buyback-7y10y-2026-09-17) and no CASH-MANAGEMENT one, yet at $12.5B this single operation is larger than every long-end operation on the whole August-refunding schedule combined — the two long-end buckets cap at $2B each even before sb0607's 09-09 doubling to at least $4B. A cash-management buyback is Treasury spending down a cash balance rather than supporting liquidity in an off-the-run sector, so it is the fiscal leg of the term-premium story showing up as an actual dated operation, which is exactly what the proposing ledger's supply-leg thesis has otherwise had to infer from the Monthly Treasury Statement. It is the second in a series: an identically-sized 1Mo-2Y cash-management operation ran 2026-09-03 (announce 09-02, settle 09-04) and was likewise untracked. TWO CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER RESEARCHES IT. First, the sector is 1Mo-2Y — it buys nothing at any tenor the long-end ledgers care about, so it is a cash/bill-supply signal, not duration support; impact is filed low for that reason despite the headline size. Second, a $12.5B cap is a ceiling and this bucket's realised fills are not measured here. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
